wholePhysicalScope: The named 58-vertex museum envelope and mapped parts distinguish both stone wings, their roofs and links, and the nine sloped subvolumes that express the five interlocking Crystal forms. The archived named McLaughlin Planetarium footprint controls its separate podium.
lodDetails: Four levels retain both stone wings, the interlocking Crystal and former planetarium. Closer levels refine the diagonal glazing, masonry, roof and entrance geometry.
limitations: The model depicts the 2015 museum complex, including the former planetarium. It predates later plaza changes and demolition of the planetarium.
The mapped outlines, heights and roof bearings control the masses. Some cantilever angles, glazed facet seams, fenestration and unphotographed elevations are estimates.
The original terrain remains unchanged. The building and pavement contacts use approximate local elevations.
